messages.subject: Possible designs
messages.body_plain:
Dear MSstats crew,

Let's assume I performed the following biological experiment:

Mice of two genotype (wt and receptor k.o. animals) were randomly assigned to two treatments: The first group received a daily injection of receptor agonist, the second a placebo. The two treatments were procured for 5 or 14 days. Each animal was sacrificed at the end of the treatment period and proteins were extracted from a tissue of interest and quantified in a label-free MS experiment.

Now I would like to answer the following scientific questions:

Which of the proteins is regulated (directly or indirectly) by the agonist application, and which protein regulation is dependent on the canonical receptor pathway?

According to MSstats manual, MSstats requires the user to provide the information on treatments in the "condition" variable. Therefor I would need to combine the information on the 3 above experimental factors into a single "hybride" factor (I will use some pseudo R code for illustration):

C <- factor(genotype:treatment:time)

Assuming a reduced scope of biological replication the LM fitted by MSstats will be:

Y_jl = u + C_j + e_jl (_ should indicate a subscribt index)

with u (intercept term) and C being a fixed effect term and e the random residual error.

To make it simple, I also assumed a single feature per protein, so F_i and (F x C_ij) are not informative. If I understand this correctly, such a model allows to estimate the treatment effect for each levels of C, …but my experimental design was aiming to look for the conditional effect of treatment by genotype (treatment|genotype). So my naive choice would rather have been to fit:

y_jl = u + genotype * treatment + time + e_jl

Now my provocative question: Is this "complex design" to much for MSstats?
If not, how would the correct 10-column format input for MSstats look like?
Since you describe MSstats as wrapper for lm(), how does the resulting lm() model formula actually look like for that case?
Is it possible to include additional blocking factors (random effects), who's estimation are not of primary interest (sex, cages)?
What happens if experimental factors are very unbalanced (e.g. condition level 1 gets 10 observations and level 2 only 3)? Would there be a warning, or would MSstats use a different estimation method for the model parameters?
Cheers,
Tobias

Dr. Sc. ETH Tobias Kockmann
Institute of Molecular Health Sciences
ETH Zurich HPL F17.2
Otto-Stern-Weg 7, 8093 Zürich, Switzerland
Phone: +41 44 633 33 91
Fax: +41 44 633 14 23
E-Mail: tobias....@biol.ethz.ch

messages.subject: pvalue equal to 0
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,
I have found that some of my proteins gives a pvalue and adj.pvalue equal to 0. I guess that this is because MSstats (or one of the dependencies) is rounding up a very small number. This is a little annoying when it comes to graphical visualization (e.g., -log10 of 0 in volcano plot can not be displayed). My workaround was to replace 0 by a very small number, but I don't want to 'replace' values after a statistical test. Does anyone know a way to avoid these 0's??

Thank you everyone,
Alex

messages.subject: Re: pvalue equal to 0
messages.body_plain:
This is floating-point underflow and it's not really avoidable--as you suspect, it comes from calculating p-values that are too small for the computer to represent. So on the plus side, you have some very significant ratios!

When I'm calculating -log p-values I usually will replace -log(zero) with -log(smallest non-zero p-value) + 1 or something like that. That is, you want to signal that the p-value is lower than the lowest non-zero value you see, but also allow it to be visible and not shockingly far from the rest of your data. As long as you document this, it's a totally reasonable thing to do.

messages.body_plain: This is a good advice. It is very common to replace very large values of -log(p-value) by a constant. This indicates that the true values are above the limit of the y axis of the graph.

messages.body_plain:
Dear Brett,

I think that the reason is that there could have multiple measurement for certain run and certain feature. When I worked with maxquant data, I found that there are several measurements in certain run and certain feature. However, MSstats assume that there is only one measurement in certain run and certain feature. MSstats.daily v3.0.1 at msstats.org <http://msstats.org> has new function for transforming MaxQuant output to MSstats input format. This function takes care of this issue. (use highest or mean measurement in certain run and certain feature, if there are multiple measurements). I hope this function can solve this issue. If you still had this error, please let me know.

- Meena

messages.body_plain:
Dear Grace,

MSstats detects technical replicates if there are different 'Run' IDs with the same 'Sample' IDs in the same condition. For example,

Condition    BioReplicate  Run
group1           sample1      run1
group1           sample1      run2
group1           sample1      run3

easy way to check the correct annotation or not, please use the line below. could you try this first?

unique(skyline.MSstats.export.MS2[,c("Condition","BioReplicate","Run")]

(If you are not sure, please send me the output of commend above.)

hope to be helpful.

-Meena

messages.subject: Re: Error help
messages.body_plain:
Hi Brett,
Assuming that your problem is what Meena suggests, i.e. multiple measurements for a given feature in a single run, I guess you are using the evidence.txt table. Particularly, I have been using the peptide.txt table instead of evidence.txt. As you may know, peptide table aggregates all charge states, thus you should have a single for each peptide sequence. In R, you will have to 'melt' the peptide table though. And then, you just create the columns PrecursorCharge, FragmentIon, ProductCharge, and IsotopeLabelType.

If you still want to use the evidence.txt table, then I would use the "Modified.sequence" column as PeptideSequence and the "Charge" column as PrecursorCharge. If your data comes from a single LC-MS/MS analysis, then the combination of Modified.sequence and Charge should be unique, AFAIK. However, if you have multiple fractions then as Meena suggests you are likely to have multiple repeated features. In this case, you have 3 options: (1) use "aggregate" function of R to aggregate these multiple features (I use 'sum' for it); (2) use "paste" function to concatenate "Modified.sequence" with "Fraction"; and (3) use the column "Fraction" as it was the column ProductCharge (I never tried, but I guess it would work).

Best,
Alex

messages.subject: Issues with duplicate entries
messages.body_plain:
I've encountered several problems with MSStats in Skyline Daily 64-bit (v3.1.7317). First, I have received an error message saying I have duplicate entries for the same peptide. I tried removing duplicate peptides and this didn't fix things. In tracking through the list of alleged multiple entries, it appears that MSstats views peptides with oxidized methionine as duplicate entry for the non-oxidized version. Is this what's happening, or have I missed another problem with my file? If this is the case, is there a way to resolve the issue? (side note: I'm more worried about implications for other post-translational modifications.)

Once I removed peptides containing oxidized methionine, I received another (unrelated?) error message: Error : Results must be all atomic, or all data frames. What does this mean, and how do I resolve the issue? Thanks in advance!

Cheryl
